cards.prose: The one who went about all Galilee teaching and healing has not changed his work by crossing over into Judaea. The synagogues are behind him now, but the kingdom is still what he preaches, and the sick are still what he heals as he goes.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew 4:23 shows the work he began in Galilee, teaching, preaching the kingdom and healing the people, which he carries across the Jordan.
cards.flag: No thread is anchored on 19:1; placed in the marriage thread because it is the verse that leads into 19:3. Loose pair.

cards.prose: Joshua was told to arise and go over this Jordan into the land given to the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and Yahusha (Jesus) bears the same name. Matthew has him come into the coasts of Judaea *beyond Jordan*, on the road Joshua first walked.
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Joshua the son of Nun
cards.member_sentence: After Moses dies, Yahuah (the LORD) tells Joshua to cross the Jordan into the land given to the children of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.flag: No thread is anchored on 19:1; placed in the marriage thread by position. Loose pair.

cards.prose: Asked about putting away a wife, he goes back past the schools to the first making. *Made them male and female* is the line in Genesis, and the whole answer to the Pharisees is going to stand on it.
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) made man in his own image, male and female, and that first making is the ground Yahusha (Jesus) answers from.

cards.prose: He answers the Pharisees with the words of the creation itself, the man leaving father and mother, cleaving to his wife, and the two becoming one flesh. That is the beginning he sends them back to, and a bill of divorcement was never where the matter started.
cards.member_sentence: The first marriage, a man leaving his father and mother to cleave to his wife as one flesh, is the beginning he appeals to.

cards.prose: Malachi sets the wife of a man's youth beside the altar. Yahuah (the LORD) stands *witness between thee and the wife of thy youth*, and she is *the wife of thy covenant*. The same chapter says he *hateth putting away* (Malachi 2:16), which is the weight behind Yahusha's (Jesus's) answer.
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (LORD) hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) is witness between a man and the wife of his youth, and she is his companion and the wife of his covenant.
cards.flag: The old note's line is Malachi 2:16, two verses past the target; the card keeps 2:14 and brings the 2:16 words in with their citation.

cards.prose: Paul reaches for the same creation word Yahusha (Jesus) uses and shows how heavy it is. The two becoming one flesh is a thing done in the body, so heavy that even a joining to a harlot makes *one body*.
cards.member_sentence: Paul quotes the one flesh of Genesis to show that a union of two bodies is a real joining, not a light thing.

cards.prose: Paul takes the same sentence from Genesis, *they two shall be one flesh*, and writes it into his teaching to husbands and wives. Then he calls it *This is a great mystery* (Ephesians 5:32) when he turns to the Messiah (Christ). The words he rests on are the words Yahusha (Jesus) rested on.
cards.member_phrase: shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh
cards.member_sentence: Paul repeats the creation sentence, a man joined to his wife and the two one flesh, as the ground for how husbands and wives live.
cards.flag: The KJV of 5:32 says 'the church'; the card does not lean on that word and keeps to the Genesis sentence Paul is quoting.

cards.prose: This is the bill the Pharisees hold up. Moses is writing around something already happening, and the paper he asks for goes into the woman's hand. Yahusha (Jesus) names it plainly, *because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives* (Matthew 19:8), a concession and not a word set above the beginning.
cards.member_phrase: then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand
cards.member_sentence: Moses wrote a bill of divorcement into the law to govern a thing that was already being done, not to make it a right.

cards.prose: Moses speaks of a king the same way. The people will say they want a king *like as all the nations that are about me*, and Moses writes the rules for that king before there is one. The hand that wrote the law of divorce wrote the law of the king, and neither was where it began.
cards.member_phrase: and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me
cards.member_sentence: Moses sets rules for a king the people will ask for like the nations, the same kind of allowance made because of the people's hearts.

cards.prose: When the elders asked for *a king to judge us like all the nations*, Yahuah (the LORD) told Samuel, *they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me* (1 Samuel 8:7). It was granted, and still it was a turning from the way. That is the shape of the bill of divorcement, *but from the beginning it was not so* (Matthew 19:8).
cards.member_phrase: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations
cards.member_sentence: Yashar'el's (Israel's) elders ask for a king like the nations, and it is allowed even though it is a turning from Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.prose: On the mountain it was *It hath been said*, and here the Pharisees bring it, but the line is the same bill of divorcement. Both times he is dealing with the easy exit men had made of it, and here he names *except it be for fornication* as the one exception.
cards.member_sentence: The Sermon quotes the same bill of divorcement and answers it, as Yahusha (Jesus) answers the Pharisees here.

cards.prose: Mark gives the same saying and says plainly where the wrong lands. The man who puts away his wife and marries another commits adultery *against her*. The weight is on what is done to the wife.
cards.member_sentence: Mark records the same saying and adds that the adultery is committed against the wife who was put away.
cards.flag: Mark has no exception clause; Matthew's 'except it be for fornication' stands as written.

cards.prose: Luke puts this saying right after *easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail* (Luke 16:17). So the word on divorce comes as the law standing, not as the law set aside.
cards.member_sentence: Luke gives the same saying on divorce straight after the word that not one tittle of the law will fail.

cards.prose: Paul hands the saying back to the one who said it. *Let not the wife depart from her husband* is not his own opinion, he says, it is Yahusha's (Jesus's) word to the married, and he goes on to say *let not the husband put away his wife* (1 Corinthians 7:11).
cards.member_sentence: Paul gives Yahusha's (Jesus's) own word to the married, that the wife is not to depart from her husband and the husband not to put her away.

cards.prose: The disciples say it is not good to marry, and Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of eunuchs. Isaiah had already spoken to the eunuch who says *I am a dry tree*, and Yahuah (the LORD) gives the one who keeps his sabbaths *a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters* (Isaiah 56:5).
cards.member_phrase: neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) tells the eunuch he is no dry tree, and will give him a name better than sons and daughters.

cards.prose: When the disciples say it is not good to marry, he answers *All men cannot receive this saying, save they to whom it is given* (Matthew 19:11). Paul says the same from his own place, that *every man hath his proper gift of Elohim (God)*, one this way and another that. The gift is given, not claimed.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says each man has his own gift from Elohim (God), one married and another not, as Yahusha (Jesus) says the saying is given to some.

cards.prose: Paul gives the reason a man might hold back from marrying, *He that is unmarried careth for the things that belong to* Yahusha (Jesus). It is the ground Yahusha (Jesus) gives for those who *have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven’s sake* (Matthew 19:12), a choice for the work and not a charge against marriage.
cards.member_phrase: He that is unmarried careth for the things that belong to Yahusha (Lord)
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the unmarried man cares for the things of Yahusha (Jesus), the reason Yahusha (Jesus) gives for those who stay single for the kingdom.

cards.prose: Revelation shows a company kept single for him, *These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth*, firstfruits *redeemed from among men*. It stands beside the eunuchs Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of as a calling given to some.
cards.member_phrase: These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth
cards.member_sentence: John sees a company kept apart for the Lamb, following him wherever he goes, as firstfruits redeemed from among men.
cards.flag: Loose pair; the card holds to what Revelation 14:4 says and does not make it an argument about marriage.

cards.prose: In chapter 18 the disciples asked *Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?* and he stood a little child in front of them. Now they are rebuking the people who bring the children, as though the answer had never been given.
cards.member_sentence: The disciples asked who was greatest, and Yahusha (Jesus) set a little child in the middle of them as the answer.

cards.prose: Mark tells it almost word for word. They brought young children so that he would *touch* them, and the disciples rebuked those who brought them. Matthew says he was to *put his hands on them, and pray*, and the point is the same, the children are carried to him and the disciples stand in the way.
cards.member_sentence: Mark tells the same scene, the children brought to be touched and the disciples rebuking those who brought them.

cards.prose: Luke says *infants*, where Matthew says *little children*, so the ones carried to him were very small. The people bring them to be touched, and the disciples again turn them back.
cards.member_sentence: Luke tells the same scene with infants carried to him and the disciples rebuking them.

cards.prose: The psalm says Yahuah (the LORD) ordains strength *Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings*, and the disciples are rebuking the babes. What they are keeping from him is what the psalm says his strength is built from.
cards.member_sentence: The psalm says strength is ordained from the mouth of babes and sucklings, the little ones the disciples were turning away.

cards.prose: Isaiah's picture of the kingdom ends with *a little child shall lead them*. The disciples treat the children as something in the way of Yahusha (Jesus), while Isaiah sets a child at the head of the wolf and the lamb under the one who judges with righteousness.
cards.member_phrase: and a little child shall lead them
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's kingdom has the wolf dwelling with the lamb and a little child leading them.

cards.prose: The young man asks what he must do to have life, and Moses had already set the answer before the people, *life and good, and death and evil*. So when Yahusha (Jesus) says *if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments* (Matthew 19:17), he is not handing out something new, he is pointing at the old road to the same life.
cards.member_sentence: Moses sets life and good beside death and evil before the people and ties life to keeping the commandments.

cards.prose: The young man asks what to do in order to live, and Leviticus has the plain answer, the statutes and judgments, *which if a man do, he shall live in them*. Yahusha (Jesus) does not send him anywhere else. He says to keep the commandments.
cards.member_sentence: Leviticus says the man who does Yahuah's (the LORD's) statutes and judgments shall live in them.

cards.prose: Ezekiel has Yahuah (the LORD) say it himself of the day he brought them out of Egypt, that the statutes he gave are ones a man does and *shall even live in them*. The young man asked what to do for life, and this is what was given for life.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) says of the statutes he gave out of Egypt that a man who does them shall even live in them.

cards.prose: Proverbs says of instruction, *keep her; for she is thy life*. The young man wants life and Yahusha (Jesus) points him to the commandments, so the two answers stand together. What Yahuah (the LORD) gave to keep is the life the man was asking for.
cards.member_sentence: Proverbs tells the son to hold fast to instruction and keep it, because it is his life.

cards.prose: *Keep my commandments, and live* is Yahusha's (Jesus's) whole answer in a single line of Proverbs. The young man asked what good thing to do for life, and the proverb says what: keep the commandments, and hold the law *as the apple of thine eye*.
cards.member_sentence: Proverbs says in one line to keep the commandments and live, and to hold the law as the apple of the eye.

cards.prose: The match is in the next verse, not this one. At Cana his mother tells the servants *Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it* (John 2:5), and the young man is asking the same Master what to do. What he says to him is to keep the commandments.
cards.member_sentence: At Cana his mother tells the servants to do whatever he says, as the young man is now told what to do.
cards.flag: Target John 2:3 (no wine at Cana) does not carry the point; the old note's 'the 1234 of Truth' is 1 John 2:3-4, so the pair may be mis-pointed (1 John 2:3 intended). I drew on John 2:5 from the context.

cards.prose: Revelation closes where the young man began. He asked how to enter into life, and its last chapter blesses *they that do his commandments*, with *right to the tree of life*. Yahusha (Jesus) said to keep the commandments, and the end of the book still says it.
cards.member_phrase: Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life
cards.member_sentence: Revelation blesses those who do his commandments with right to the tree of life and entry into the city.

cards.prose: Every commandment he names to the young man is a word from Sinai, and this is the one he adds after the four, *Honour thy father and thy mother*. When he says to keep the commandments, these are the commandments he means, the ones spoken by Yahuah (the LORD), not a new list.
cards.member_phrase: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land
cards.member_sentence: The fifth commandment, to honour father and mother with long days in the land, is the one Yahusha (Jesus) adds to his list.

cards.prose: He ends his list with love of neighbour, and he takes it from Leviticus, *thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself*, where it stands among the statutes and closes with *I am Yahuah (LORD)*. The young man is given Moses from the first word to the last.
cards.member_sentence: Leviticus holds the word to love your neighbour as yourself, spoken in the name of Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.prose: Deuteronomy gives the fifth word again as Moses repeats it to the people, *as Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath commanded thee*. The commandments Yahusha (Jesus) lists are the ones the Torah says twice, and he sets them before the young man as they stand.
cards.member_phrase: Honour thy father and thy mother, as Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath commanded thee
cards.member_sentence: Moses repeats the command to honour father and mother, as Yahuah (the LORD) commanded, that it may go well in the land.

cards.prose: Perfect is the same word in both places. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the young man *if thou wilt be perfect*, and in the Sermon it is *Be ye therefore perfect*. In both it is the whole heart toward the Father, standing on the commandments, never above them or past them.
cards.member_sentence: The Sermon calls his hearers to be perfect as their Father in heaven is perfect, the same word he gives the young man.

cards.prose: *Walk before me, and be thou perfect* is what Yahuah (the LORD) said to Abram as he was about to make his covenant with him, long before Sinai. So Yahusha's (Jesus's) *if thou wilt be perfect* is not a step above the commandments. It is the fathers' own call, to walk whole before him.
cards.member_phrase: walk before me, and be thou perfect
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) tells Abram to walk before him and be perfect, long before Sinai.

cards.prose: Moses puts it in one line, *Thou shalt be perfect with Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)*, and puts it among the commandments to Yashar'el (Israel), not over them. So when Yahusha (Jesus) says *if thou wilt be perfect*, he is using Moses' word.
cards.member_sentence: Moses tells the people to be perfect with Yahuah (the LORD) their Elohim (God), apart from the ways of the nations.

cards.prose: He says to his disciples what he said to the young man, *Sell that ye have, and give alms*, with the same reward, *a treasure in the heavens*. It was not a trap set for one rich man, and Luke puts the heart right behind it, *For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also* (Luke 12:34).
cards.member_sentence: Luke has the same word to sell and give alms and lay up a treasure in the heavens that fails not.

cards.prose: In Acts the multitude who believed were *of one heart and of one soul* and had *all things common*. What he asked of the young man, to sell and give, was done freely by many who followed him.
cards.member_sentence: Acts shows the believers of one heart and soul holding all things common, as Yahusha (Jesus) asked the young man to part with his goods.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says a rich man shall *hardly enter*, and Proverbs has a man praying against that weight, *give me neither poverty nor riches*. He asks for enough and no more.
cards.member_sentence: A man in Proverbs asks Yahuah (the LORD) for neither poverty nor riches, only the food he needs.

cards.prose: Jeremiah sets the rich man beside the wise man and the mighty man and says none of them should boast. Yahusha's (Jesus's) word about the rich man is the same warning, *let not the rich man glory in his riches*, said sharper, and the needle shows how close the glory sits to the heart.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) tells the wise, the mighty and the rich not to glory in their wisdom, might or riches.

cards.prose: The psalm names the man in Yahusha's (Jesus's) saying, those who *trust in their wealth*, and then says what the wealth cannot buy, *None of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to Elohim (God) a ransom for him* (Psalm 49:7). Riches do not carry a man into the kingdom, and that is the trouble the disciples feel.
cards.member_sentence: The psalm names those who trust in their wealth, and says none of them can redeem a brother.

cards.prose: James speaks to the rich the way the prophets did, *weep and howl for your miseries*. Yahusha (Jesus) says it will be hard for a rich man to enter, and James names the sorrow coming on those who stayed there, the same warning in a plainer voice.
cards.member_sentence: James tells the rich to weep and howl for the miseries coming on them.

cards.prose: Paul says why. *They that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare*, into lusts that *drown men in destruction and perdition*. He does not blame the money but the wanting of it, and Yahusha's (Jesus's) rich man with his needle has the same trouble.
cards.member_phrase: they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare
cards.member_sentence: Paul says those who want to be rich fall into a snare and into lusts that drown men in destruction.

cards.prose: To the disciples' *Who then can be saved?* the answer is an old one. Sarah was told she would have a son, and the word that went with it was *Is any thing too hard for Yahuah (LORD)?* What man cannot do, he has done before.
cards.member_phrase: Is any thing too hard for Yahuah (LORD)? At the time appointed I will return unto thee
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) asks whether anything is too hard for him, when a son is promised to Sarah.

cards.prose: Jeremiah prays it as a confession, *there is nothing too hard for thee*, and gives the proof, the heaven and the earth made by *great power and stretched out arm*. The disciples' question is answered by the one who made everything.
cards.member_phrase: thou hast made the heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm, and there is nothing too hard for thee
cards.member_sentence: Jeremiah confesses that the maker of heaven and earth, by his great power, has nothing too hard for him.

cards.prose: Jeremiah prayed that nothing was too hard for him, and the answer now comes from Yahuah (the LORD) himself, *the Elohim (God) of all flesh*, asking it back, *is there any thing too hard for me?* The disciples' question has met the one for whom it is not impossible.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD), the Elohim (God) of all flesh, himself asks whether anything is too hard for him.

cards.prose: Job comes out of his trial saying *I know that thou canst do every thing*, which is where the disciples have to arrive. The question of who can be saved is not answered by what a man can do.
cards.member_sentence: Job confesses that Yahuah (the LORD) can do everything and that no thought is hidden from him.

cards.prose: Luke puts the same sentence at the opening of his gospel, *For with Elohim (God) nothing shall be impossible*, before anything he did on earth was seen. Yahusha (Jesus) says it to the disciples after the camel and the needle, and it is the same promise.
cards.member_sentence: Luke records that with Elohim (God) nothing shall be impossible, the same word Yahusha (Jesus) gives the disciples.

cards.prose: The impossible thing is answered by a gift. Ezekiel has Yahuah (the LORD) take away *the stony heart* and give *an heart of flesh*, so the one who could not keep the commandments is made able to, as the next verse says, *cause you to walk in my statutes* (Ezekiel 36:27).
cards.member_phrase: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new heart and a new spirit in place of the stony heart, doing what man cannot.

cards.prose: Daniel sees *one like the Son of Adam* brought near the Ancient of days, and the next verse gives him a kingdom, *his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away* (Daniel 7:14). When Matthew's Son of Adam sits *in the throne of his glory*, it is that kingdom given, with the twelve seated under him.
cards.member_phrase: one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days
cards.member_sentence: Daniel sees one like the Son of Adam come to the Ancient of days to receive the everlasting kingdom.

cards.prose: Matthew gives the throne a second time, *the Son of Adam shall come in his glory*, and then *sit upon the throne of his glory*. It is the same throne the twelve thrones stand beside in this chapter, and the judging rests on it.
cards.member_phrase: then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory
cards.member_sentence: Matthew places the Son of Adam coming in his glory and sitting upon the throne of his glory.

cards.prose: *In the regeneration* is the word in Matthew, and Isaiah is the promise behind it, *I create new heavens and a new earth*. The next verse names the people in it, *I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy* (Isaiah 65:18). The throne is set in that renewed world.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) creates new heavens and a new earth, the renewing Matthew calls the regeneration.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) says the new heavens and the new earth *shall remain before me*, and then *so shall your seed and your name remain*. The renewing Matthew speaks of is bound up with a seed that stays, and the twelve tribes under the thrones are that seed.
cards.member_sentence: The new heavens and new earth remain before Yahuah (the LORD), and so does the seed and name of his people.

cards.prose: Acts says the same day in other words. The heaven must keep him *until the times of restitution of all things*, which Elohim (God) *hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets*. Matthew's regeneration is that restoring, and the prophets were already speaking of it.
cards.member_sentence: The heaven holds him until the times of restitution of all things, spoken by all the holy prophets since the world began.

cards.prose: Paul counts the sufferings of this time small beside *the glory which shall be revealed in us*, and says creation waits for *the manifestation of the sons of Elohim (God)* (Romans 8:19). Those who left all to follow him in Matthew are looking at the same day.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the sufferings of this time are not worth comparing with the glory to be revealed in those who follow him.

cards.prose: In Revelation John sees what the regeneration leads to, *a new heaven and a new earth*, with the first ones passed away. Matthew gives the moment the Son of Adam takes his throne, and Revelation shows the world made new.
cards.member_phrase: I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away
cards.member_sentence: John sees a new heaven and a new earth, the first ones passed away, the world made new that Matthew's regeneration points to.

cards.prose: The twelve thrones sit over the twelve tribes, and in Revelation the city has *twelve gates*, with the *names of the twelve tribes* written on them. The tribes are still named tribes at the end, as in Matthew, and never a word for something else.
cards.member_phrase: names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: The city's twelve gates carry the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.prose: The city that carries the tribes' names on its gates carries *the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb* on its foundations. It sets the twelve who followed him beside the twelve tribes they judge, as Matthew does, one set of twelve beside the other and neither taking the other's place.
cards.member_sentence: The wall of the city has twelve foundations with the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.

cards.prose: John sees *four and twenty seats* round a throne, with elders sitting on them *clothed in white raiment*, crowned. Seats round a throne is the picture Matthew gives of the twelve, though how many of these seats are the tribes and how many the apostles is something the verse does not say.
cards.member_phrase: round about the throne were four and twenty seats: and upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment
cards.member_sentence: Twenty-four seats stand round the throne, with elders in white and crowns on them.
cards.flag: The old note read the 24 elders as twelve tribes plus twelve apostles; the verse does not say it, so I left it as an open working reading.

cards.prose: This verse only opens the word, and the word is the two sticks, *take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Yahudah (Judah)* (Ezekiel 37:16), and the other for Joseph, and both *become one in thine hand* (Ezekiel 37:17). The twelve tribes the twelve are set over are the two houses made one.
cards.member_sentence: The word of Yahuah (the LORD) comes again to Ezekiel, opening the vision of the two sticks joined into one.
cards.flag: The target verse is only the opening formula; the point is carried by 37:16-17 from the context.

cards.prose: Isaiah has Yahuah (the Lord) set his hand again *to recover the remnant of his people* from Assyria, Egypt and the islands of the sea, the whole scattering named. Those he recovers are the ones the twelve thrones are set over, so the tribes in Matthew are people brought home, not a figure of speech.
cards.member_phrase: set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the Lord) sets his hand a second time to recover the remnant of his people from every place they were scattered.

cards.prose: The new covenant is made *with the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* and with the house of Yahudah (Judah), both houses. The twelve tribes in Matthew are the same two houses, and the covenant that brings them in is the one Jeremiah says is made with them.
cards.member_phrase: I will make a new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and with the house of Yahudah (Judah)
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new covenant with both the house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah).

cards.prose: Ezekiel's closing vision starts at the house in a restored land, where *waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward*. The twelve thrones belong to that same renewed day, and it is the same restored land the tribes come home to.
cards.member_sentence: Ezekiel's vision of the restored land begins at the door of the house with waters flowing from under the threshold.
cards.flag: Weak pair: the old note speaks of the tribes' land allotment, but this verse is only the river from the house; 47:13 onward is not in my packet.

cards.prose: James writes his letter *to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad*, so the apostles after the resurrection still speak of twelve tribes, scattered, as a people to be written to. They are the tribes the thrones are set over, real and still scattered, which is why the gathering matters.
cards.member_phrase: to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting
cards.member_sentence: James addresses his letter to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, treating them as a real people still.

cards.prose: Paul says *our twelve tribes* hope to come to the promise, and he says it before a king as the hope he is accused for. The twelve tribes are a living people in his mouth, *instantly serving Elohim (God) day and night*, and Matthew's thrones are set over them.
cards.member_phrase: our twelve tribes, instantly serving Elohim (God) day and night, hope to come
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the twelve tribes, serving Elohim (God) day and night, hope to come to the promise.

cards.prose: Paul asks *Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?* as something the people ought already to know. It is the judging of the thrones in Matthew carried into his letter, those who followed him given a part in the judging.
cards.member_sentence: Paul reminds the Corinthians that the saints shall judge the world.

cards.prose: John sees *thrones* with those seated on them *and judgment was given unto them*, and those who sat held to the witness of Yahusha (Jesus), refused the mark, and reigned with Messiah (Christ). That is the seated company Matthew promises to those who followed him.
cards.member_phrase: I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them
cards.member_sentence: John sees thrones with those who held to the witness of Yahusha (Jesus) seated on them, judging and reigning with Messiah (Christ).

cards.prose: Luke has the same promise and gives the reason for it, *Ye are they which have continued with me in my temptations*. The thrones come after the staying with him, *sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Luke 22:30), and in both gospels it is the twelve tribes who are judged.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) tells those who stayed with him in his trials that a kingdom is appointed them, with thrones over the twelve tribes.

cards.prose: The promise of the hundredfold is followed straight away by the householder who went out early to hire labourers, and the parable takes up the saying that closes the chapter, *many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first* (Matthew 19:30). The reward is promised, and the vineyard shows whose hand it comes from.
cards.member_phrase: the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers
cards.member_sentence: The parable of the householder hiring labourers into his vineyard follows and works out the saying that the first shall be last.

cards.prose: Mark lists the same losses, house, brethren, father, mother, wife, children, lands, and sets a second reason beside Matthew's *my name’s sake*, *for my sake, and the gospel’s*. It is the same promise to anyone who leaves what he has for the one who calls.
cards.member_phrase: no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands
cards.member_sentence: Mark records the same promise to those who have left house, family and lands for his sake and the gospel's.

cards.prose: Luke gives the reason in different words, *for the kingdom of Elohim's (God’s) sake*, where Matthew has *my name’s sake*. The two belong together, because to leave all for his name is to leave all for the kingdom he preaches.
cards.member_phrase: no man that hath left house, or parents, or brethren, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of Elohim's (God’s) sake
cards.member_sentence: Luke records the same promise to those who left house, family and children for the kingdom of Elohim (God).

cards.prose: The psalm sets the house of Elohim (God) against a lifetime elsewhere, *a day in thy courts is better than a thousand*, and a doorkeeper's place better than a tent of wickedness. The one who gives up houses and lands for his name has weighed it the same way, and the hundredfold answers that weighing.
cards.member_phrase: I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my Elohim (God), than to dwell in the tents of wickedness
cards.member_sentence: A day in the courts of Elohim (God) is better than a thousand, and a doorkeeper's place better than the tents of wickedness.
